security_audit.summary: The audit confirms serious install and persistence risks, including a remote installer executed through bash, user-level AI tool hooks, and automatic project source modification. Many markdown, localhost, and status-check matches were false positives, but the remaining confirmed behavior is enough to require manual review before publishing. No direct credential exfiltration intent was found. Static review was capped at 400/850 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 450 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.
Replace curl-to-bash install paths with pinned packages, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation before execution.
Move hooks to opt-in per-project configuration where possible, show an exact diff, and provide a complete uninstall command.
Require an interactive diff review before installing agentation or changing application source files.
Rewrite imperative mode-switching text as scoped guidance and remove instructions that tell agents to proceed without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary files and local service assumptions
remediation.suggestion: Use private per-session temp directories, validate file ownership, and fail closed when localhost services are unavailable.

content.user_title: Coordinate AI Agent Workflows with JEO
content.value_statement: Complex AI coding sessions need consistent planning, verification, and handoff controls. JEO provides a cross-tool workflow for plan review, execution, UI feedback, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Tracks workflow phase and approval state in a project state file.
Configures integrations for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
Runs plannotator plan review loops and records approval or feedback.
Supports agentation-based UI annotation review through local MCP or HTTP flows.
Checks installed tools and reports missing workflow components.
Provides worktree cleanup helpers after an agent workflow finishes.
limitations: Requires git, Node 18 or later, bash, Python, and optional external CLIs.
Setup scripts can change user-level AI tool configuration files.
Browser and annotation flows require a running app and reachable localhost services.
Plan gates can fail in sandboxes that block local port binding.

use_cases.title: Structure a coding workflow
use_cases.description: Create a plan gate, execution phase, verification step, and cleanup step for a coding task.

use_cases.title: Review browser UI changes
use_cases.description: Run browser verification and collect submitted UI annotations before resolving feedback.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent setup
use_cases.description: Install similar orchestration behavior across several AI coding tools.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a small task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use JEO to plan this task first, then wait for plan approval before implementation: <task>.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a UI change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use JEO to implement this UI change, verify the page in a browser, and summarize the visible result.

prompt_templates.title: Process UI annotations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use JEO annotate mode after I submit UI annotations. Acknowledge each item, apply fixes, and report what changed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the workflow setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the JEO setup for this repository. Identify which hooks, prompts, local services, and cleanup steps are active.

output_examples.input: Plan a login form update with JEO.
output: The workflow enters PLAN phase and records the task state.
A plan review gate is prepared before implementation begins.
Execution waits for approval or feedback before moving forward.

output_examples.input: Use JEO to verify a dashboard change.
output: The implementation is checked with browser verification tools.
The result includes observed UI state and remaining issues.
Cleanup guidance is provided after verification finishes.

output_examples.input: Run annotate mode after I submit UI feedback.
output: Submitted annotations are listed and acknowledged.
Each fix is applied, then marked resolved with a short summary.
The loop stops when no submitted annotations remain.

best_practices: Run setup scripts with dry-run first and review every configuration change.
Use JEO only in trusted repositories where local hooks are expected.
Keep localhost services private and stop them when the workflow ends.
anti_patterns: Do not run the full installer in an untrusted repository.
Do not let the skill auto-modify application entry points without reviewing the diff.
Do not treat generated plan approval as a replacement for human review on sensitive work.

faq.question: What does JEO coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates planning, execution, browser verification, UI annotation review, and cleanup across several AI coding tools.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex, with files also describing Gemini CLI and OpenCode setup.

faq.question: Does it install external tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Several setup paths use npm, npx, plugin commands, or installer scripts for external components.

faq.question: Does it change user configuration?
faq.answer: Yes. Setup scripts can write Claude, Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode configuration files in the user home directory.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Some flows use local HTTP services, package registries, plugin marketplaces, or remote installer URLs.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic marketplace install?
faq.answer: No. The audit identifies persistent hooks, remote installers, and automatic source modification that require manual review.
